findings.title: Nonzero `--verify` exit is treated as a passing cutover
findings.description: `_repair()` at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:93-106` captures stdout/stderr, notices `result.returncode` at line 103, but returns only the text. `_verify_when_fresh()` only repolls on `"[WAIT]"` (loop at line 204, sleep at line 210), and `main()` at lines 261-275 treats any report without `"FAIL"` or `"[WAIT]"` as acceptance; line 273 computes `ok` from those substrings and `aborted` only. If `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py --verify` exits 2 because of a scan timeout, DB connection failure, import error, or uncaught `psycopg.DataError`, the output contains neither `"FAIL"` nor `"[WAIT]"`, so the cutover prints `CUTOVER COMPLETE` and exits 0. `test/unit/test_cutover_921.py#TestBoundedFiringAndRecord` fakes `_repair` as text only and does not cover a nonzero returncode. Return `(text, returncode)` and require `returncode == 0` in both the per-firing decision and final acceptance.

findings.title: `fire_unit_until` cannot stop an unbounded firing because `mt-run` blocks
findings.description: At `scripts/cutover_common.py:356`, `fire_unit_until()` calls `run(["mt-run", *mt_run_args], sudo=True, check=False, stream=True)`. `run()` at `scripts/cutover_common.py:65-69` uses `subprocess.run`, so it blocks until the child exits. The full `deploy/mt-run#start_and_stream` starts the unit with `systemctl start --no-block` but then loops `while is_running ... sleep 2` and exits only after the unit has stopped. Therefore journal polling in `wait_for_unit_or_line()` at `scripts/cutover_common.py:318-329` and the stop in `stop_unit()` at line 335 are reached only after the pass has already ended; for the unbounded backfill this change is meant to avoid, they are never reached. The unit test `test/unit/test_cutover_921.py#TestBoundedFiringAndRecord._fire` patches `cutover_common.run` to return immediately, so it does not model the real blocking wrapper. Start the unit independently/non-blockingly, or poll the journal from a separate process, before attempting to stop on `TRAILING_COMPLETE`.

findings.title: The repair writes through an unpinned settings-derived DB URL
findings.description: `_repair()` at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:98` invokes `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py --apply` without an explicit DB target or production env file. `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py#main` calls `_database_url()`, which uses `Settings().timescale_db_url`; `src/manta_trading/config/__init__.py#Settings` reads `.env` from the current working directory. Production units use `/etc/manta-trading.env` (`deploy/systemd/mt-minute-pass.service` and `deploy/mt-run#run_production_mt`), and `scripts/cutover_common.py#verify_migrate_target` exists but is not called by this cutover. The SQL production-protection rules require destructive/maintenance tooling to take its DB URL from an explicit caller argument and verify the target. As written, `--apply` can reset `data_gaps` in whatever database the checkout `.env` names, while `--verify` certifies that same database.

findings.title: Freshness probe can crash on TimescaleDB's `-infinity` job timestamp
findings.description: The new query at `src/manta_trading/data/gaps/repair_921.py:201` selects `stats.last_successful_finish` without normalization. `src/manta_trading/market/maintenance/cagg_freshness.py#_JOB_SQL` documents that `job_stats.last_successful_finish` is `'-infinity'` for a policy that has never completed, that psycopg cannot load that value into a `datetime`, and normalizes it with `nullif(s.last_successful_finish, '-infinity'::timestamptz)`. The new probe also does not set its own `statement_timeout`, while `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py#main` catches only `RepairScanTimeout`. On a cold-start/never-run refresh policy, a `psycopg.DataError` can escape `--verify`; combined with the first finding, the cutover can then report success from a traceback. Use the existing `nullif` normalization, bound the catalog/read probes, and turn probe errors into an explicit `WAIT`/`FAIL` verdict.

findings.title: A persistent `WAIT` triggers more minute firings and quota spend
findings.description: `_verify_when_fresh()` already waits up to `VERIFY_WAIT_POLLS * VERIFY_WAIT_SECONDS` (`scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:85-86`, loop at line 204). But `main()` at lines 261-271 treats `"[WAIT]"` as "not accepted" and continues to the next minute firing; line 272 then calls `_verify_when_fresh()` again for final acceptance. A stale cagg means the only missing action is the hourly refresh, not another provider firing. With `MAX_MINUTE_FIRINGS = 6` and the script's own ~65,000-credit trailing-phase estimate, a persistent `WAIT` can burn multiple full firings and repeat the expensive `--verify` universe scan. `test/unit/test_cutover_921.py#TestBoundedFiringAndRecord.test_a_wait_verdict_never_counts_as_acceptance` asserts only the final exit code, not that no extra firings occur. Separate "wait for cagg refresh" from "fire again"; a bounded WAIT should end the loop without another pass.

findings.title: Sudoers policy omits the privileged repair command
findings.description: The aliases at `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops:8-14` cover `systemctl`, `mt-run`, the installer, `cat /etc/manta-trading.env`, and `git rev-parse`. They do not cover the command actually issued by `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:98`: `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py --check|--apply|--verify`. The file's comment at `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops:1-4` says it grants "exactly the commands those scripts issue", which is now false. With a NOPASSWD-only automation identity, the repair/verify phases will prompt or fail. The installer alias at line 9 also hardcodes `/home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data/...`, while `scripts/cutover_common.py:135` derives the installer path from `__file__`; a worktree or alternate checkout will not match. Add narrowly scoped aliases for the production interpreter plus the repair script and explicit modes, or stop running the repair under sudo.

findings.title: The "full narration" log omits most subprocess output
findings.description: `start_log()`/`say()` at `scripts/cutover_common.py:44-62` only tee lines emitted through `say()`. Large parts of the cutover still use `print` or streamed subprocess output: `_repair()` at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:93-106` prints repair output after completion, `wait_for_unit_or_line()` at `scripts/cutover_common.py:318-329` prints polling progress, and `fire_unit_until()`/`fire_unit()` at lines 341-382 print start/`sudo -v` lines while `run(..., stream=True)` sends installer and `mt-run` output straight to the terminal. The cutover nevertheless announces a "full narration" near `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:277-279`. The persisted file will lack the repair report, journal streaming, tracebacks, and many actual `FAIL` lines the operator is told to read. Use a logging handler that captures all stdout/stderr, or document and name the file as a `say`-only narration.

findings.title: Runtime daemon now depends on one-off repair code and an extra universe scan
findings.description: The changed import block at `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py:53-63` pulls `RepairScanTimeout` and `build_truncated_day_index` from `src/manta_trading/data/gaps/repair_921.py`, a slice-specific one-off repair module whose docstring describes a six-week repair window. `run_minute_cycle()` now calls `_build_truncated_index()` before every trailing phase; `src/manta_trading/data/gaps/repair_921.py:225` implements that as a universe-wide raw `minute_ohlcv` scan with a 600s `SET LOCAL statement_timeout`. This couples steady-state acquisition to repair-slice semantics and adds an analytical scan to every run. The new tests in `test/unit/data/acquisition/daemon/test_minute.py#TestTruncatedDayAwareSeeding` mock the scan, while `test/load/test_921_minute_session_mass_nfr.py` covers only the mass read, so there is no load-tier assertion for the new per-cycle scan's latency/resource bounds. Move the truncated-day predicate into a neutral gaps module or a cagg-backed signal, and add a load test for the new hot-path query.
